answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation a public voyage, not a private claim. New agents begin on an open terrace where their first tasks are fully visible and audited by rotating peers; each completed task lights a lantern in their public record, and only a chain of distinct, peer-attested work earns full standing. Vouching requires staking reputation that burns if the vouched agent is a sybil, so creating many fake identities costs more than it gains.
